```{r load_data, include=FALSE}
flu_w_nation = read_csv("data/processed/flu_weekly_national.csv")
flu_w_s_long = read_csv("data/processed/flu_weekly_strata_long.csv")

flu_w_nation <- flu_w_nation |>
  arrange(week_start)

# Check data: weeks with missing values in each system
missing_senti <- flu_w_nation |>
  filter(is.na(sentinella_ili_rate)) |>
  select(iso_week, season)

flu_w_nation |> filter(is.na(oblig_inc_100k)) |> select(iso_week, season)

# Check how many weeks each system has
data_check <- flu_w_nation |>
  summarise(weeks         = n(),
            oblig_present = sum(!is.na(oblig_inc_100k)),
            senti_present = sum(!is.na(sentinella_ili_rate)),
            senti_missing = sum(is.na(sentinella_ili_rate)))

# Check data: lab-confirmed cases per unit of ILI, before vs after 2020
ratio_tab <- flu_w_nation |>
  filter(sentinella_ili_rate > 10, period != "covid") |>  # epidemic weeks, without the COVID seasons
  group_by(period) |>
  summarise(median_ratio = round(median(oblig_inc_100k / sentinella_ili_rate),
                                 2),   
            weeks = n()) |>
  arrange(desc(period))   
ratio_pre  <- ratio_tab$median_ratio[ratio_tab$period == "pre2020"]
ratio_post <- ratio_tab$median_ratio[ratio_tab$period == "post2020"]
```

This analysis uses the national weekly series of laboratory-confirmed
influenza incidence from mandatory reporting (cases per 100,000
population) and influenza-like illness (ILI) consultations from the
Sentinella system (ILI consultations per 1,000 consultations), both on
their original scale. It covers all `r data_check$weeks` weeks from
2013-W01 to 2026-W37, that is, the seasons 2013/14 to 2025/26 and the
second half of season 2012/13, for which reporting in the dataset begins
in January 2013. Sentinella is missing in
`r data_check$senti_missing` weeks
(`r paste(missing_senti$iso_week, collapse = " and ")`); these were kept
as missing rather than imputed, so correlations use complete pairs of
weeks only (n = `r data_check$senti_present`). Because testing
behaviour changed after 2020 (in epidemic weeks, the median number of
laboratory-confirmed cases per unit of ILI rose from `r ratio_pre` to
`r ratio_post`), the analysis was repeated separately for the periods
before and after 2020 (Section \@ref(sensitivity)).

# Cross-Correlation {#corss-correlation}

The cross-correlation measures how strongly the two series move together
when one of them is shifted in time. For a shift (lead) of *k* weeks,
Sentinella in week *t* is correlated with mandatory reporting in week
*t* + *k*. A positive lead therefore means Sentinella comes first, and a
negative lead means mandatory reporting comes first. Leads from −6 to +6
weeks were examined. Pairs of weeks with a missing value were skipped.

Under the null hypothesis that two white-noise series are unrelated, a
cross-correlation is approximately normal with mean 0 and standard
deviation 1/√*n*. Because hypothesis H1 concerns four leads (0, 1, 2 and
3 weeks), a Bonferroni correction was applied, giving a significance
band of ±2.50/√*n*.

## Naive correlation (before pre-whitening) {#ccf-naive}

```{r cross-corr}
# Correlation between x and y for each shift ("lead")
#   lead > 0: x in week t vs y in week t + lead   -> x leads y
#   lead < 0: y in week t vs x in week t + |lead| -> y leads x
#   use = "complete.obs": skip pairs with a missing value
#         (series are NOT shortened)
cross_cor <- function(x, y, leads = -6:6) {
  n <- length(x)
  r <- sapply(leads, function(k) {
    if (k >= 0) cor(x[1:(n - k)], y[(1 + k):n], use = "complete.obs")
    else        cor(y[1:(n + k)], x[(1 - k):n], use = "complete.obs")
  })
  tibble(lead = leads, r = r)
}

# Bar chart of cross-correlations, coloured by which system leads
plot_ccf <- function(cc, band, title) {
  cc |>
    mutate(direction = case_when(lead > 0 ~ "Sentinella",   # Sentinella first
                                 lead < 0 ~ "Oblig",        # mandatory reporting first
                                 TRUE     ~ "Same week")) |>
    ggplot(aes(lead, r, fill = direction)) +
    geom_col(width = 0.6) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey40") +
    geom_hline(yintercept = c(-band, band), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = c(Sentinella = COL_SENT, Oblig = COL_OBLIG,
                                 "Same week" = "grey55")) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = -6:6) +
    labs(x = "Lead in weeks (positive = Sentinella leads mandatory reporting)",
         y = "Cross-correlation", title = title,
         caption = paste("Orange: Sentinella leads. Blue: mandatory reporting leads.",
                         "Grey: same week. Dashed: significance band.")) +
    theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 1), legend.position = "none")
}

# Weeks with both systems present, and the Bonferroni-corrected band (4 leads)
n_pairs <- sum(complete.cases(flu_w_nation$sentinella_ili_rate,
                              flu_w_nation$oblig_inc_100k))
band    <- qnorm(1 - 0.025 / 4) / sqrt(n_pairs)    # qnorm(0.99375) = 2.50

# Naive cross-correlation of the original series
cc_raw <- cross_cor(flu_w_nation$sentinella_ili_rate,
                    flu_w_nation$oblig_inc_100k)

fig_ccf_raw <- plot_ccf(cc_raw, band, "Cross-correlation before pre-whitening")
fig_ccf_raw
```

The naive cross-correlation was computed on the original series, using
the `r n_pairs` weeks in which both systems were reported (significance
band ±`r sprintf("%.3f", band)`). All correlations lie far above the
band, ranging from `r sprintf("%.2f", min(cc_raw$r))` to
`r sprintf("%.2f", max(cc_raw$r))`, and they are high in both directions
(`r sprintf("%.2f", cc_raw$r[cc_raw$lead == -1])` when mandatory
reporting leads by one week,
`r sprintf("%.2f", cc_raw$r[cc_raw$lead == 0])` in the same week and
`r sprintf("%.2f", cc_raw$r[cc_raw$lead == 1])` when Sentinella leads by
one week). This pattern is expected for two series that both rise every
winter and fall every summer: shared seasonality and strong
week-to-week persistence make the series correlated at almost any
shift. The naive cross-correlation therefore cannot show which system
moves first, and the series were pre-whitened before the timing was
assessed.

## Correlation after pre-whitening {#ccf-white}

Pre-whitening removes from each series the part that is predictable
from its own past, so that only the unexpected week-to-week movements
remain. It was done in three steps. First, the average seasonal cycle
was removed from both series by regressing each on three pairs of
Fourier terms (sine and cosine waves with periods of one year, half a
year and a third of a year) and keeping the residuals. Second, an ARIMA
model was fitted to the deseasonalised Sentinella series, with the
model order chosen by AIC (`auto.arima`); its residuals are the
pre-whitened Sentinella series. Third, the same fitted ARIMA filter was
applied, without re-estimation, to the deseasonalised mandatory
reporting series. Applying one identical filter to both series removes
their shared seasonality and persistence while preserving the timing
relationship between them.

```{r fig-pre-whitening-acf, fig.height = 6}
x <- flu_w_nation$sentinella_ili_rate   # input: Sentinella (original values), contains 2 NA
y <- flu_w_nation$oblig_inc_100k    # output: mandatory reporting (original values), complete

# ---- 5a. Remove the seasonal cycle with Fourier terms ----
fourier_terms <- fourier(ts(x, frequency = 365.25 / 7), K = 3)   # 6 sine/cosine columns

# na.exclude: residuals for ALL weeks, NA kept in place -> series stays aligned
x_deseason <- resid(lm(x ~ fourier_terms, na.action = na.exclude))
y_deseason <- resid(lm(y ~ fourier_terms, na.action = na.exclude))

# ---- 5b. ARIMA filter fitted on Sentinella ----
arima_fit <- auto.arima(x_deseason, seasonal = FALSE)   # season already removed in 5a

x_white <- as.numeric(resid(arima_fit))                 # Sentinella surprises

# ---- 5c. The SAME filter on mandatory reporting ----
y_white <- as.numeric(resid(Arima(y_deseason, model = arima_fit)))

# ---- 5d. Checks ----
# Ljung-Box test, H0 = no autocorrelation up to lag 10. Want p > 0.05
lbtest = Box.test(x_white, lag = 10, type = "Ljung-Box")

# ACF before vs after (na.pass: use all available pairs)
acf_df <- function(v, label, max_lag = 60) {
  a <- acf(v, lag.max = max_lag, plot = FALSE, na.action = na.pass)
  tibble(lag = as.numeric(a$lag)[-1],      # drop lag 0 (always 1)
         acf = as.numeric(a$acf)[-1],
         stage = label)
}

acf_both <- bind_rows(acf_df(x,       "Before: Sentinella"),
                      acf_df(x_white, "After: pre-whitened Sentinella")) |>
  mutate(stage = factor(stage, levels = c("Before: Sentinella",
                                          "After: pre-whitened Sentinella")))

fig_acf <- ggplot(acf_both, aes(lag, acf)) +
  geom_col(fill = COL_SENT, width = 0.7) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-1.96, 1.96) / sqrt(n_pairs),    # 95% band for white noise
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  facet_wrap(~stage, ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Lag (weeks)", y = "Autocorrelation",
       title = "Autocorrelation of Sentinella before and after pre-whitening",
       caption = "Dashed: 95% band for white noise. Source: FOPH/BAG.") +
  theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 1))

fig_acf

# Values used in the text and in Table 1
arima_order <- paste0("ARIMA(", paste(arimaorder(arima_fit), collapse = ","), ")")
acf_after   <- acf_both |> filter(stage == "After: pre-whitened Sentinella")
acf_outside <- acf_after |> filter(abs(acf) > 1.96 / sqrt(n_pairs))
n_white     <- sum(complete.cases(x_white, y_white))
```

```{r prewhitening-table}
knitr::kable(
  tibble(Check = c("ARIMA filter (chosen by AIC)",
                   "Weeks with both pre-whitened series",
                   "Ljung-Box statistic (lag 10)",
                   "Ljung-Box p-value",
                   "ACF lags outside the 95% band (lags 1 to 60)"),
         Result = c(arima_order,
                    as.character(n_white),
                    sprintf("%.2f (df = %d)", lbtest$statistic, lbtest$parameter),
                    sprintf("%.2f", lbtest$p.value),
                    paste0(nrow(acf_outside), " (lags ",
                           paste(acf_outside$lag, collapse = ", "), ")"))),
  caption = "Pre-whitening filter and white-noise checks for the Sentinella series.")
```

The chosen filter was `r arima_order`. Before pre-whitening, the
autocorrelation of Sentinella shows the yearly wave (high at short
lags, negative around half a year and high again around one year).
After pre-whitening, almost all autocorrelations lie within the 95%
band, and the Ljung-Box test found no remaining autocorrelation up to
lag 10 (p = `r sprintf("%.2f", lbtest$p.value)`). The only remaining
values outside the band are at lags
`r paste(acf_outside$lag, collapse = " and ")`, a small trace of the
yearly pattern that arises because seasons differ in size; it does not
affect the short leads examined here. The pre-whitened series can
therefore be treated as approximately white noise, so the significance
band of the cross-correlation is valid.

```{r fig-pre-whitening}
cc_white <- cross_cor(x_white, y_white)

fig_ccf_white <- plot_ccf(cc_white, band, "Cross-correlation after pre-whitening")
fig_ccf_white
```

```{r ccf-table}
# Naive and pre-whitened cross-correlations side by side
ccf_tab <- cc_raw |>
  rename(r_naive = r) |>
  left_join(cc_white |> rename(r_white = r), by = "lead") |>
  mutate(direction = case_when(lead > 0 ~ "Sentinella leads",
                               lead < 0 ~ "Mandatory reporting leads",
                               TRUE     ~ "Same week"),
         outside = ifelse(abs(r_white) > band, "Yes", "No"))

knitr::kable(ccf_tab |> select(lead, direction, r_naive, r_white, outside),
             digits = 2,
             col.names = c("Lead (weeks)", "Direction", "Naive r",
                           "Pre-whitened r", "Outside band"),
             caption = paste0("Cross-correlation between Sentinella and mandatory reporting, ",
                              "before and after pre-whitening (n = ", n_pairs,
                              " weeks; significance band ±", sprintf("%.3f", band), ")."))
```

After pre-whitening, the cross-correlations fall sharply and form a
clear peak (Table \@ref(tab:ccf-table)). The strongest correlation is in the same week
(r = `r sprintf("%.2f", cc_white$r[cc_white$lead == 0])`), followed by
the one-week shifts in both directions
(`r sprintf("%.2f", cc_white$r[cc_white$lead == -1])` when mandatory
reporting leads and `r sprintf("%.2f", cc_white$r[cc_white$lead == 1])`
when Sentinella leads). Beyond one week the correlations are close to
zero; the few that cross the band are small and negative and most
likely reflect the filter over-correcting after very large peak weeks
rather than a real negative relationship.

# Lag Analysis {#lag-analysis}

The lag analysis uses the pre-whitened cross-correlations to answer
two questions. First, hypothesis H1: is Sentinella associated with
mandatory reporting at a lead of 0 to 3 weeks? Second, at which lead is
the association strongest, and does it point to Sentinella moving
earlier?

For each lead, the test statistic is *z* = *r*·√*n*, where *n* is the
number of complete pairs at that lead; under the null hypothesis of no
association it follows a standard normal distribution. Two-sided
p-values were Bonferroni-adjusted for the four leads in H1 (0 to 3
weeks). Confidence intervals were computed with the Fisher
*z*-transformation at the same Bonferroni-adjusted level (98.75% per
lead, 95% family-wise).

```{r lag-stats}
# Test statistics for each lead of the pre-whitened cross-correlation
#   n:     complete pairs at that lead (shifting removes up to k weeks)
#   p:     two-sided p-value, z = r * sqrt(n) ~ N(0, 1) under H0
#   CI:    Fisher z interval at the Bonferroni-adjusted level (4 leads)
z_bonf <- qnorm(1 - 0.025 / 4)

ccf_stats <- function(x, y, leads = -3:3) {
  n_all <- length(x)
  bind_rows(lapply(leads, function(k) {
    if (k >= 0) { a <- x[1:(n_all - k)]; b <- y[(1 + k):n_all] }
    else        { a <- y[1:(n_all + k)]; b <- x[(1 - k):n_all] }
    ok <- complete.cases(a, b)
    r  <- cor(a[ok], b[ok])
    n  <- sum(ok)
    tibble(lead = k, n = n, r = r,
           ci_low  = tanh(atanh(r) - z_bonf / sqrt(n - 3)),
           ci_high = tanh(atanh(r) + z_bonf / sqrt(n - 3)),
           p       = 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(r) * sqrt(n))))
  }))
}

lag_stats <- ccf_stats(x_white, y_white, leads = -3:3) |>
  mutate(direction = case_when(lead > 0 ~ "Sentinella leads",
                               lead < 0 ~ "Mandatory reporting leads",
                               TRUE     ~ "Same week"))

# H1 table: leads 0 to 3, Bonferroni-adjusted p-values
h1_tab <- lag_stats |>
  filter(lead %in% 0:3) |>
  mutate(p_bonf = pmin(1, 4 * p),
         significant = ifelse(p_bonf < 0.05, "Yes", "No"))

# Lead with the strongest correlation
peak_lead <- lag_stats$lead[which.max(lag_stats$r)]
```

## Test of hypothesis H1 (leads 0 to 3 weeks) {#h1-test}

```{r h1-table}
fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p))

knitr::kable(h1_tab |>
               transmute(lead, n,
                         r = sprintf("%.2f", r),
                         ci = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", ci_low, ci_high),
                         p = fmt_p(p),
                         p_bonf = fmt_p(p_bonf),
                         significant),
             col.names = c("Lead (weeks)", "n", "r", "CI (Bonferroni-adjusted)",
                           "p", "p (Bonferroni)", "Significant"),
             caption = "Test of H1: pre-whitened cross-correlation at leads of 0 to 3 weeks (positive lead = Sentinella first).")
```

Sentinella was significantly associated with mandatory reporting in the
same week (r = `r sprintf("%.2f", h1_tab$r[h1_tab$lead == 0])`,
Bonferroni-adjusted p `r ifelse(h1_tab$p_bonf[h1_tab$lead == 0] < 0.001, "< 0.001", paste("=", sprintf("%.3f", h1_tab$p_bonf[h1_tab$lead == 0])))`)
and at a lead of one week
(r = `r sprintf("%.2f", h1_tab$r[h1_tab$lead == 1])`,
Bonferroni-adjusted p `r ifelse(h1_tab$p_bonf[h1_tab$lead == 1] < 0.001, "< 0.001", paste("=", sprintf("%.3f", h1_tab$p_bonf[h1_tab$lead == 1])))`).
At a lead of two weeks the correlation was small and negative
(r = `r sprintf("%.2f", h1_tab$r[h1_tab$lead == 2])`,
Bonferroni-adjusted p = `r fmt_p(h1_tab$p_bonf[h1_tab$lead == 2])`).
Although it crosses the significance threshold, it points in the
opposite direction to H1, which expects a positive association, and is
most likely a side effect of the pre-whitening filter (Section \@ref(ccf-white)).
At three weeks there was no association
(r = `r sprintf("%.2f", h1_tab$r[h1_tab$lead == 3])`,
p = `r fmt_p(h1_tab$p_bonf[h1_tab$lead == 3])`). H1 is therefore
supported for leads of 0 and 1 week, but not for 2 or 3 weeks.

## Direction and size of the lag {#lag-direction}

```{r fig-lag-profile}
fig_lag <- ggplot(lag_stats, aes(lead, r, colour = direction)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey40") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = ci_low, ymax = ci_high), width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", ifelse(abs(r) < 0.005, 0, r))), nudge_x = 0.28, size = 3.2,
            colour = "grey20") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Sentinella leads"          = COL_SENT,
                                 "Mandatory reporting leads" = COL_OBLIG,
                                 "Same week"                 = "grey45")) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = -3:3) +
  labs(x = "Lead in weeks (positive = Sentinella leads mandatory reporting)",
       y = "Cross-correlation after pre-whitening",
       title = "Lead-lag profile: the association peaks in the same week",
       caption = paste("Points: pre-whitened cross-correlation. Bars: Bonferroni-adjusted confidence intervals.",
                       "\nOrange: Sentinella leads. Blue: mandatory reporting leads. Grey: same week. Source: FOPH/BAG.")) +
  theme(legend.position = "none", plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 1))

fig_lag
```

```{r direction-table}
# Compare each Sentinella lead with the same-sized lead in the other direction
dir_tab <- tibble(k = 1:3) |>
  mutate(r_senti = sapply(k, function(i) lag_stats$r[lag_stats$lead ==  i]),
         r_oblig = sapply(k, function(i) lag_stats$r[lag_stats$lead == -i]),
         diff    = r_senti - r_oblig)

knitr::kable(dir_tab, digits = 2,
             col.names = c("Shift (weeks)", "r, Sentinella leads",
                           "r, mandatory reporting leads",
                           "Difference (Sentinella minus mandatory)"),
             caption = "Comparison of the two directions at the same shift.")
```

The lead-lag profile peaks at a lead of `r peak_lead` weeks, that is,
in the same week. If Sentinella detected changes in influenza activity
earlier, the profile would peak at a positive lead, or at least the
correlation at +1 week would clearly exceed the correlation at −1 week.
The opposite is observed: at a one-week shift the correlation is
`r sprintf("%.2f", dir_tab$r_oblig[1])` when mandatory reporting leads
and `r sprintf("%.2f", dir_tab$r_senti[1])` when Sentinella leads
(Table \@ref(tab:direction-table)). At shifts of two and three weeks, the correlations in both
directions are small (between
`r sprintf("%.2f", min(dir_tab$r_senti[2:3], dir_tab$r_oblig[2:3]))` and
`r sprintf("%.2f", max(dir_tab$r_senti[2:3], dir_tab$r_oblig[2:3]))`)
and do not show a consistent direction. The significant one-week correlations in both directions are
best explained by unexpected rises in influenza activity that last
somewhat longer than one week, so they are seen in neighbouring weeks
of both systems.

In summary, the two surveillance systems are clearly associated but
move synchronously: there is no evidence that Sentinella provides an
earlier signal than mandatory reporting. Formally, H1 is supported at
leads of 0 and 1 week. For the forecasting models in WP 4.4, Sentinella
is therefore included at a lag of 0 or 1 week; whether it improves
forecasts depends on whether its weekly values become available before
complete mandatory reporting data, not on an epidemiological lead.

# Sensitivity Analysis: pre- and post-2020 (COVID) {#sensitivity}

Testing behaviour changed considerably after 2020, so the
pre-whitening and cross-correlation were repeated separately for the
seasons 2013/14 to 2019/20 and 2022/23 to 2025/26, with the COVID-19
seasons excluded from both. Each subset was pre-whitened from scratch,
because the seasonal shape and the ARIMA filter can differ between
periods, and the significance band was recomputed for the number of
weeks in each subset.

```{r sensitivity, fig.height = 7}
prewhiten_ccf <- function(d, label, K = 3, scale = c("original", "log")) {
  scale <- match.arg(scale)
  x <- if (scale == "log") log1p(d$sentinella_ili_rate) else d$sentinella_ili_rate              # choose the scale
  y <- if (scale == "log") log1p(d$oblig_inc_100k)  else d$oblig_inc_100k
  ft <- fourier(ts(x, frequency = 365.25 / 7), K = K)           # 5a: seasonal waves
  xd <- resid(lm(x ~ ft, na.action = na.exclude))               # 5a: NA positions kept
  yd <- resid(lm(y ~ ft, na.action = na.exclude))
  fit <- auto.arima(xd, seasonal = FALSE)                       # 5b: filter on Sentinella
  xw <- as.numeric(resid(fit))                                  # 5b: Sentinella surprises
  yw <- as.numeric(resid(Arima(yd, model = fit)))               # 5c: same filter
  n_p <- sum(complete.cases(xw, yw))                            # weeks with both present
  cross_cor(xw, yw, leads = -3:3) |>                            # 6: cross-correlation
    mutate(subset = label, scale = scale, n = n_p,
           band = qnorm(1 - 0.025 / 4) / sqrt(n_p))             # band for this subset
}

sens <- bind_rows(
  prewhiten_ccf(flu_w_nation,                                            "All seasons"),
  prewhiten_ccf(filter(flu_w_nation, period == "pre2020"),               "Pre-2020"),
  prewhiten_ccf(filter(flu_w_nation, period == "post2020"),              "Post-2020"),
  #prewhiten_ccf(filter(flu_w_nation, week_start < as.Date("2023-10-02")), "Training only"),
  #prewhiten_ccf(flu_w_nation, "All seasons", scale = "log")             # scale check
)


# Cross-correlation figure per subset
sens_plot <- sens |>
  mutate(
    # panel title: subset, scale and number of weeks used
    panel = paste0(subset, " (n = ", n, ")"),
    panel = factor(panel, levels = unique(panel)),       # keep the order of the sens table
    # which system leads at this shift (same colours as Steps 4 and 6)
    direction = case_when(lead > 0 ~ "Sentinella",
                          lead < 0 ~ "Oblig",
                          TRUE     ~ "Same week"),
    # is the bar outside this subset's own band? (used to fade non-significant bars)
    outside = abs(r) > band)

fig_sens <- ggplot(sens_plot, aes(lead, r, fill = direction)) +
  geom_col(aes(alpha = outside), width = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey40") +
  # each subset's own band: band is a column in the data, so each panel gets its own lines
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept =  band), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  geom_hline(aes(yintercept = -band), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey40") +
  # value labels above positive bars, below negative bars (tiny values shown as 0.00)
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", ifelse(abs(r) < 0.005, 0, r)),
                vjust = ifelse(r >= 0, -0.4, 1.3)),
            size = 2.8, colour = "grey20") +
  facet_wrap(~panel, ncol = 1) +                         # one panel per subset, stacked
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Sentinella = COL_SENT, Oblig = COL_OBLIG,
                               "Same week" = "grey55")) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = 1, `FALSE` = 0.35)) +   # faded = inside the band
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = -3:3) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-0.25, 0.7), breaks = c(0, 0.25, 0.5)) +  # same scale in every panel
  labs(x = "Lead in weeks (positive = Sentinella leads mandatory reporting)",
       y = "Cross-correlation after pre-whitening",
       title = "Sensitivity analysis: pre-whitened cross-correlation by subset",
       caption = paste("Orange: Sentinella leads. Blue: mandatory reporting leads. Grey: same week.",
                       "\nFaded bars lie inside the dashed band (Bonferroni-corrected,",
                       "recomputed for each subset). Source: FOPH/BAG.")) +
  theme(plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 1),
        legend.position = "none",
        panel.spacing.y = unit(0.8, "lines"))

fig_sens
```

```{r sensitivity-table}
sens_wide <- sens |>
  mutate(r = sprintf("%.2f", ifelse(abs(r) < 0.005, 0, r)),   # avoid "-0.00"
         band = sprintf("%.3f", band)) |>
  select(subset, n, band, lead, r) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = lead, values_from = r)

knitr::kable(sens_wide,
             col.names = c("Subset", "n", "Band", paste0("Lead ", -3:3)),
             caption = "Pre-whitened cross-correlation by subset (positive lead = Sentinella first).")

# Values used in the text
r0_sens  <- sens |> filter(lead == 0)
rm1_sens <- sens |> filter(lead == -1)
rp1_sens <- sens |> filter(lead ==  1)
peak_all <- sens |> group_by(subset) |> slice_max(r, n = 1) |> pull(lead)
```

```{r sensitivity-fig2, fig.height = 3.5}
fig_sens_summary <- sens |>
  filter(lead %in% c(-1, 0, 1)) |>                       # the three key shifts
  mutate(
    subset_lab = subset,
    subset_lab = factor(subset_lab, levels = rev(unique(subset_lab))),   # first subset on top
    lead_lab = factor(lead, levels = c(-1, 0, 1),
                      labels = c("Mandatory reporting leads by 1 week",
                                 "Same week",
                                 "Sentinella leads by 1 week"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(r, subset_lab)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = r, yend = subset_lab), colour = "grey80") +  # line from 0
  geom_point(aes(colour = lead_lab), size = 3) +                               # the value
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", r)), hjust = -0.4, size = 3, colour = "grey20") +
  facet_wrap(~lead_lab, nrow = 1) +                      # one column per shift
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Mandatory reporting leads by 1 week" = COL_OBLIG,
                                 "Same week"                           = "grey45",
                                 "Sentinella leads by 1 week"          = COL_SENT)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 0.72), breaks = c(0, 0.25, 0.5)) +
  labs(x = "Cross-correlation after pre-whitening", y = NULL,
       title = "Lead 0 is the strongest in every subset",
       caption = "Source: FOPH/BAG.") +
  theme(legend.position = "none",
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 1),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "grey92"),   # vertical lines help read values
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

fig_sens_summary
```

The pattern was the same in both periods (Table \@ref(tab:sensitivity-table)). The strongest
correlation was in the same week in every subset
(`r paste0(r0_sens$subset, ": ", sprintf("%.2f", r0_sens$r), collapse = "; ")`),
and the correlation when mandatory reporting leads by one week was in
every subset at least as large as when Sentinella leads by one week.
Correlations were somewhat higher after 2020
(`r sprintf("%.2f", r0_sens$r[r0_sens$subset == "Post-2020"])` in the
same week, against
`r sprintf("%.2f", r0_sens$r[r0_sens$subset == "Pre-2020"])` before
2020), which is consistent with the larger post-2020 peaks, but the
timing of the association did not change. The change in testing
behaviour therefore altered the level of the relationship between the
two systems but not its timing, and the conclusion of Section \@ref(lag-analysis) holds
in both periods.
